gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic volatility and subnational fiscal distress caused by oil price collapses may constrain state-level implementation capacity and domestic public funding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide 100 percent IDA credit financing for total project costs without requiring mandatory counterpart cash contributions from participating state governments.
gen_risks.evidence: The collapse of oil prices and the liquidity crunch revived tensions between federal government and subnational governments regarding burden of the adjustment

gen_risks.description: Militancy and security instability in regions such as the Niger Delta and North East could disrupt field supervision, infrastructure works, and agricultural supply chains.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt flexible state/cluster resource allocation, conduct local security assessments, and rely on community-level engagement for project implementation.
gen_risks.evidence: sharp drop in oil production levels due to militant activities in the Niger Delta region.

gen_risks.description: Delays in executing and securing legal opinions for Subsidiary Agreements between the Federal Government and participating states may delay project effectiveness and disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce disbursement conditions requiring authorized subsidiary agreements and satisfactory legal opinions prior to releasing funds to any participating state.
gen_risks.evidence: No withdrawal shall be made under Categories (1), (2), and (3)... unless the Association has received an opinion

gen_risks.description: Financial management weaknesses regarding unretired travel advances and inadequate documentation in PFMUs and FPFMD could cause ineligible expenditures and audit qualifications.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an enhanced accountability framework in the Financial Procedures Manual, including risk-based internal audits and strict advance acquittal enforcement.
gen_risks.evidence: The key issues noted within the PFMUs and FPFMD are unretired advances and inadequate documentation of the eligible expenditures incurred.

gen_risks.description: Weak procurement capacity in state coordination offices and required executive approval thresholds at state levels could cause procurement delays and slippages.
gen_risks.mitigation: Competitively recruit qualified procurement specialists, hire a technical procurement consultant to support state offices, and utilize standardized national bidding documents.
gen_risks.evidence: The procurement capacity is still considered low and most of the states do not have procurement tools in place.

gen_risks.description: Agricultural intensification and increased usage of agro-chemicals (pesticides, synthetic fertilizers) could lead to soil contamination, surface water pollution, and health hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an Integrated Pest Management Plan (IPMP) and ESMF screening procedures to promote climate-smart agriculture and safe pesticide handling.
gen_risks.evidence: agricultural intensification involving the use of inputs, could potentially have adverse impact on soil, water and vegetation covers.

gen_risks.description: Civil works for processing infrastructure, aggregation centers, and access roads may lead to land acquisition, physical displacement, or restricted access to common resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply the Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF) to screen sub-project sites and prepare Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) providing fair compensation before works begin.
gen_risks.evidence: infrastructure investments could result in involuntary re-settlement and land requisition.

gen_risks.description: Installation of utility connections, transmission lines, or gas pipelines for processing clusters could encroach upon sensitive natural habitats such as wetlands and marshes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce OP/BP 4.04 Natural Habitats screening protocols within the ESMF to ensure sub-project infrastructure avoids sensitive ecological zones.
gen_risks.evidence: extension of electricity transmission lines and installation of gas pipelines might pass through important natural habitats such as swamps and marshes.

gen_risks.description: Financial and economic viability is highly sensitive to drops in commodity market prices, where a 20 percent reduction in benefit values causes negative NPVs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop structured business alliances with off-takers, support commodity aggregation centers, and invest in primary processing to stabilize producer prices and prevent post-harvest losses.
gen_risks.evidence: if benefits were reduced by 20 percent for all the crops, the net present values will turn negative

gen_risks.description: Gender gaps in access to land, agricultural inputs, credit, and extension services could prevent female farmers and entrepreneurs from benefiting from project investments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated Women and Youth Empowerment sub-component with dedicated grant funding, business development services, mentorship, and gender-tracked M&E indicators.
gen_risks.evidence: women in Nigeria, compared with men, have relatively limited access to productive agricultural land, inputs and services.

gen_risks.description: Delays in competitively recruiting and deploying new APPEALS implementation staff from existing CADP structures could slow initial implementation momentum.
gen_risks.mitigation: Retain existing CADP operational staff using government funding during an 18-month transitional period while competitive recruitment is conducted.
gen_risks.evidence: During the first 18-month period of project implementation, it is expected that selection and replacement of CADP staff will be completed

gen_risks.description: Multi-tiered institutional arrangements across federal and state bodies (NSC, NCO, SSC, STC, SCO, PFMU) risk operational misalignment and bureaucratic bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define clear roles and responsibilities in the Project Implementation Manual, schedule structured quarterly STC and annual SSC meetings, and establish regular progress reporting.
gen_risks.evidence: Project implementation will involve both the federal and state governments. The project will be executed jointly by the NCO at the federal level and SCOs

gen_risks.description: Prevalence of adulterated or substandard agricultural inputs (seeds, fertilizers, chemicals) in local markets could severely undermine productivity gains.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to FMARD and national regulatory agencies to strengthen quality assurance, seed certification, and agro-dealer accreditation.
gen_risks.evidence: capacity strengthening on quality control of agro-inputs such as seeds, fertilizer and agro-chemicals to address issues of adulteration

gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder communication or unaddressed community grievances regarding sub-project selection and benefit distribution could result in local conflict or dissatisfaction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a comprehensive Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), implement a strategic communication and outreach campaign, and monitor citizen engagement metrics.
gen_risks.evidence: Percentage of grievances registered, related to delivery of project benefits that are actually addressed

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk has been rated Substantial. Coordination of externally funded projects' responsibilities between the federal and state levels is a complex phenomenon, and incomprehension or misinterpretation at any level can affect the project implementation negatively.
gt_risks.mitigation: A communication strategy, supported by the project, will ensure that transparency is maintained at all levels of project management and implementation, and the participation of beneficiaries remains at the core of the project.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risks are rated Substantial. Falling oil prices have undermined economic growth in the country and remain a major source of risks, which may be exacerbated further by security challenges, natural disasters, and climate change. With reliance on a few primary exports and a relatively undiversified economy, Nigeria remains vulnerable to external demand and price shocks, compounded by pressures from weak fiscal management.
gt_risks.mitigation: The World Bank is in close dialogue with the authorities on the reform program in support of restoring macro-economic resilience and economic growth.

gt_risks.description: Sector Policies and Strategies risk has been rated Substantial. One major risk is frequent changes in the agricultural policy, especially the tariff policy, which would change the economic incentives faced by farmers and the private sector alike. Considering this is a multi-sector project, risk associated with other sector policies (e.g., transport and energy) might also affect implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated through a sustained, evidence-based policy dialogue and engagement with the government to ensure sustainability of the reforms in the sector.

gt_risks.description: Technical Design risk has been rated Moderate. The approach for agribusiness partnership proposed by this project has already been successfully implemented under CADP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Lessons learned from both CADP and other similar operations have been incorporated into the project design, which is based on analyses undertaken during preparation and summarized under Annex 2.

gt_risks.description: Institutional Capacity for Implementation and Sustainability risk has been rated Substantial. While capacity at the federal level for implementing World Bank-supported agricultural project activities is adequate, there is a risk at state level of insufficient experience, structure, and technical knowhow to manage the new project design features.
gt_risks.mitigation: SCOs' staff will be provided necessary training at the time of launching the project, and newly recruited staff (particularly in Kogi state) will benefit from an induction training program. Coordination challenges will be addressed by Steering Committees at federal and state levels, and a Technical Committee at state level chaired by the Commissioner of Agriculture. NCO and SCO will collaborate with FADAMAIII, RAMP, and GEM where relevant, and the project may contract a third-party service provider to assist states in project execution.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (financial management) is assessed as Substantial. The key risks identified are those of value for money in works/construction contracts and capacity building events; capacity building activities such as training workshops have been identified as having significant fiduciary risks.
gt_risks.mitigation: Additional steps include: (i) all training and workshop activities subject to prior review by the Bank; (ii) activities part of the approved annual work plan; (iii) part of the project training plan; and (iv) compliance with the enhanced accountability framework. A qualified procurement specialist will be selected competitively; goods and consultants' services will be procured in accordance with World Bank anti-fraud/corruption guidelines and procurement guidelines.

gt_risks.description: Environment and Social risk has been rated Substantial. The Environmental Category assigned to the project is Category B, predicated on the assumption that environmental risks and social impact may not have serious adverse impact of a sensitive or diverse nature; the project may not be engaged in development of heavy infrastructure or acquisition of large expanses of land.
gt_risks.mitigation: An Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and an Integrated Pest Management Plan (IPMP) have been prepared and publicly disclosed. Specific Environment and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs) and Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) will be conducted for each public and private investment once the type of work is determined and precisely located, and a Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment will cover all areas and localities in which the project will operate.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholders/Gender risk: there is a risk that women will be disadvantaged in terms of their access to employment and participation in out-growers arrangements.
gt_risks.mitigation: A detailed gender assessment and tracking for the project will be undertaken with the DFID-supported Gender Filter Trust Fund, in collaboration with the Africa Gender Innovation Lab, and incorporated into the Project Implementation Manual. A substantial part of Component 2 (35% of project funding) will support a Women and Youth Empowerment program, with affirmation of 35 percent female inclusion in all aspects of the project (representation in joint community meetings, jobs, extension agents, facilitators, and agri-business/entrepreneurship development), plus TA and training on business plan preparation, accounting, and financial management for women.
